# Vienna 1683 – Life sciences

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from eras/europe-1683-vienna.yaml — do not edit -->

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Microorganisms (living things too small to see)** [`microorganisms`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/microorganisms.md) — K2, use none, make medium, accept medium. Leeuwenhoek's letters reach scholars through the Philosophical Transactions and learned journals. Nobody in Vienna has repeated them; he keeps his lens-making secret. A fused glass bead would do. Local: Jesuit college (Kircher's claim of worms in plague blood); spectacle makers; Sorbait, member of the Leopoldina. Elsewhere: Delft: Leeuwenhoek; London: Royal Society, Hooke.
- **Life comes only from life (spontaneous generation refuted)** [`spontaneous_generation_refuted`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/spontaneous_generation_refuted.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept low. Redi's covered-jar experiment (1668) is in print, but Aristotle and the Jesuit Kircher teach that vermin arise from decay. The test costs meat, jars and gauze. Elsewhere: Florence: Francesco Redi.
- **Fermentation is the work of living yeast** [`fermentation_yeast`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/fermentation_yeast.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Brewers and bakers pass on yeast as a substance and vintners rely on the must itself. Fermentation is explained as an inner motion of particles. Local: Bürgerspital brewery (holds the city's beer monopoly); vintners of the suburbs and Lower Austria. Elsewhere: Delft: Leeuwenhoek describes yeast globules in 1680.
- **Cell theory** [`cell_theory`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cell_theory.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. Hooke's cork 'cells' and the plant anatomy of Malpighi and Grew are curiosities in books; nobody thinks of them as units of life. Elsewhere: London: Hooke, Grew; Bologna: Malpighi.
- **Viruses (disease agents smaller than bacteria)** [`viruses`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/viruses.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept low
- **Systematic classification and naming of living things** [`taxonomy`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/taxonomy.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Plants are known from herbals and Bauhin's Pinax, ordered for the apothecary. Clusius described the Austrian and Pannonian flora while in Vienna (1573–1588). Local: medical faculty (botany taught with medicine); apothecaries' herb gardens. Elsewhere: England: John Ray; Leiden and Padua botanical gardens.
- **Egg, sperm and fertilisation** [`reproduction_fertilisation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/reproduction_fertilisation.md) — K2, use none, make hard, accept low. Harvey's 'everything from the egg', de Graaf's follicles and Leeuwenhoek's seed animalcules are in print and feed a quarrel over preformation. Teaching still follows Aristotle and Galen.
- **Heredity by discrete factors (Mendel)** [`heredity_genetics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/heredity_genetics.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Breeders and gardeners know that like begets like. Counting ratios over generations of peas takes several summers and a garden outside a besieged city.
- **Evolution by natural selection** [`evolution_natural_selection`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/evolution_natural_selection.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Species are fixed since Creation; fossils are sports of nature or relics of the Flood. Saying otherwise in a Jesuit university town invites a charge of impiety.
- **DNA is the hereditary material (double helix)** [`dna_structure`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/dna_structure.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept low
- **Breathing is slow combustion (respiration and body heat)** [`respiration_metabolism`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/respiration_metabolism.md) — K2, use none, make hard, accept medium. The air-pump deaths of animals and Lower's reddening of blood by air are known from books. The usual doctrine: breathing cools the heart and vents sooty vapours. Elsewhere: London and Oxford: Boyle, Hooke, Lower; Mayow's Tractatus (1674).
- **Plants are built from air, water and light (photosynthesis and mineral nutrition)** [`photosynthesis_plant_nutrition`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/photosynthesis_plant_nutrition.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. Van Helmont's willow is read as proof that plants are made of water. Farmers hold that plants eat the fat of the soil.
- **Legumes fix nitrogen from the air (root nodule bacteria)** [`nitrogen_fixation_biology`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/nitrogen_fixation_biology.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. That peas, beans and vetch leave land in better heart is farmers' and Columella's knowledge. Nobody has looked at the root nodules.
- **The brain and nerves (seat of thought, electrical signalling)** [`nervous_system_brain`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/nervous_system_brain.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept medium. Willis's anatomy of the brain (1664) is on the shelves. Nerves are thought to carry animal spirits; epilepsy and melancholy may still be read as possession.
